content.about: Belarus is a landlocked country in Eastern Europe, mostly flat and covered in forests, marshes and lakes. It has thousands of lakes and is sometimes called "the land of blue lakes". Its capital, Minsk, was rebuilt after the Second World War. European bison live in its forests.

standout.text: Belovezhskaya Pushcha, shared with Poland, is one of Europe's last primeval forests.

didYouKnow: Potatoes are central to Belarusian cooking.
Mir Castle is a UNESCO-listed medieval fortress.
